To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subtle sequence differences among MHC class molecules greatly influence their susceptibility to HCMV-encoded US2- and/or US11-mediated degradation.

subtle sequence variations within the cytoplasmic domain of class I HCs, and the C-terminal part of the alpha2 and alpha3 domains, greatly influence sensitivity to HCMVS2- and US1-mediated degradation.
the C-termini of MHC class molecules are crucial in US11-mediated downregulation and that US2 recognizes a small region at a junction between alpha2/alpha2 domains of the HC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of MHC class-I down-regulation by HCMV US11 and US2.
a better understanding of how HCMV US proteins interact with their target proteins.
the mechanisms of MHC class 1 down-regulation and the identification of the molecular determinants for this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
US2 and US 11 have a broad spectrum of MHC class 1 molecules they target, but that they do not have a complete spectrum of MHC molecules they target.

US2- and/or US11-mediated degradation of MHC class 1 molecules is determined by the following factors: the length of the cytoplasmic tails, the number and position of lysine residues and the number of alpha-helices in the alpha3 domains.

the sensitivity to US2- or US11-mediated degradation of MHC class 1 molecules depends on subtle sequence variation in several domains of the heavy chain, including the alpha2/ alpha3 junction and the cytoplasmic C-terminus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
US2 and US1 are more specific in their interaction with MHC class I alleles than US11 and US6.

US2 and US 11 can target MHC class I HCs for degradation by a similar, yet distinct, mechanism, and that the C-terminal domain of class I HCs is an important determinant for their sensitivity to US11-mediated degradation.
US2 and US1 are more specific than US11 for MHC class I alleles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal domain of MHC class molecules represents an important site for US11-mediated degradation, whereas US2 is more sensitive to subtle changes in the alpha2/ alpha3 junction.
the sensitivity of HCMV to US2- or US11-mediated degradation of MHC class molecules is highly dependent on the subtle differences in their amino acid sequence.

subtle sequence differences between MHC class I products are sufficient to determine their sensitivity to US2- or US11-mediated degradation, which has important implications for the development of HCMV vaccines and therapeutics.
